summary: Ukraine faces an imminent massive combined strike with 60-80 missiles including hypersonic Zircon and Iskander-M systems, while a Ukrainian F-16 was lost on July 29, 2026 during a combat interception mission. Russian Tu-95MS and Tu-160 strategic bombers are being redeployed from the Far East and Ukrainka airfield, and US and French intelligence assisted Ukraine in mapping Russian air defense positions for drone strikes on Russian territory.
key_points: A massive combined strike on Ukraine is expected with 60-80 missiles including 525 Shaheds, 38 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 31 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 9 Zircon hypersonic missiles, with elevated threats to Odesa, Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv, and other regions. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69451)

A Ukrainian Air Force F-16 fighter was lost on July 29, 2026 during a combat mission to intercept enemy aerial targets; the pilot ejected safely and was evacuated without civilian casualties. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69456)

Russian Tu-95MS strategic bombers are being redeployed from the Far East to Olenya airfield with at least one already airborne, and a total of 8 aircraft are planned for relocation. (Source: eRadarrua/103032)
Three Tu-160 bombers took off from the Ukrainka airfield, indicating ongoing Russian strategic aviation operations. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69453)
US and French intelligence helped Ukraine identify Russian air defense positions and select drone routes and targets for strikes on Russian territory. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/32025)

Overnight air defense neutralized 65 Russian UAVs, with 14 strike UAVs confirmed hitting 10 locations across Ukraine, injuring 5 people including a 3-year-old boy in Dnipropetrovshchyna. (Source: UkraineNow/82994)
Ukraine's energy infrastructure suffered 164 total strikes from July 1 to 29, with 10 energy nodes hit on July 28-29 across Crimea, Khersonshchyna, and Luhanshchyna. (Source: UkraineNow/83001)

points: A massive combined strike on Ukraine is expected with 60-80 missiles, including 525 Shaheds, 70 reactive Shaheds, 38 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 31 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, 16 Kalibr cruise missiles, 15 Banderol cruise missiles, 9 Zircon hypersonic missiles, up to 8 Kh-59 cruise missiles, 6 Kinzhal aero-ballistic missiles, and 3 Oniks cruise missiles. Elevated threat to Odesa, Kyiv, Lviv, Ivano-Frankivsk, Dnipro, Pavlohrad, and Kharkiv. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69455)

On July 29, 2026, contact was lost with a Ukrainian Air Force F-16 fighter performing a combat mission to intercept enemy aerial targets; the pilot ejected and was safely evacuated to a medical facility for examination. No civilian casualties or destruction were reported at the crash site. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69456)

Overnight, Ukrainian air defense neutralized 65 Russian UAVs; 14 strike UAVs hit 10 locations, with debris falls at 2 additional sites. In Dnipropetrovshchyna, 5 people were injured, including a 3-year-old boy, and infrastructure, a medical facility, clinic, shop, private houses, and cars were damaged. (Source: UkraineNow/82994)

From July 1 to 29, 164 energy targets were struck across Ukraine; on July 28-29 alone, 10 energy nodes were hit in the temporarily occupied territories of Crimea, Khersonshchyna, and Luhanshchyna, according to SBS commander Robert Brovdi. (Source: UkraineNow/83001)

Acting Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevgeny Khmara stated he wants to end the war within the next 14 years, saying he wants to end it before his sons reach conscription age. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/32013)

US and French intelligence helped Ukraine identify Russian air defense positions and select drone routes and targets for strikes on Russian territory, according to Financial Times reporting. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/32025)
Ukrainian President Zelensky met with Polish PM Donald Tusk in Lublin, discussing bilateral issues and security challenges for Ukrainians who fled to Poland during the war. (Source: UkraineNow/83006)

Tu-95MS strategic bombers are being redeployed from the Far East to Olenya airfield, with at least one aircraft already airborne and a total of 8 aircraft planned for relocation. Evening strategic aviation activity is being monitored. (Source: eRadarrua/103032)
Three Tu-160 bombers took off from the Ukrainka airbase, indicating ongoing Russian strategic aviation operations. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69453)

In Tula, an unknown assailant ambushed and shot three times at Andrey Cherezov, head of the company 'Russian Laboratory of Air Transport' which develops and supplies drone systems; he was hospitalized and the shooter is being sought. The company recently received contracts worth nearly 30 million rubles for UAV assembly kits and control systems. (Source: UkraineNow/82999)

The Permneftorgsintez oil refinery, one of the largest Russian oil refineries owned by Lukoil, was completely burned on July 29, 2026, under Ukraine's long-range sanctions; the facility produces aviation fuel, diesel, and high-octane gasoline and is located over 1,500 km from Ukraine's borders. (Source: eRadarrua/103054)

Russian forces are conducting drone strikes using Shaheds from Khersonshchyna toward the Black Sea waters, and reactive UAVs have been observed past Nikopol heading to Kryvyi Rih. (Source: mon1tor_ua/69447)

Russian tactical aviation activity has been noted on the southern, northeastern, and southeastern fronts, with KAB (gliding bombs) launches reported on northern Kharkivshchyna and on Donetschynna. (Source: kpszsu/70646)
The Russian army is already fighting in settlements of the Druzhkovsky urban community, according to UKR Leaks. (Source: ukr_leaks_eng/32012)

sections.threat_assessment: The threat level is significantly elevated as Russia prepares a massive combined strike involving up to 80 missiles including hypersonic Zircon and Kinzhal systems alongside 525 Shahed drones across multiple axes including Odesa, Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv, and Dnipro. Russian strategic aviation is being redeployed with Tu-95MS bombers moving from the Far East to Olenya and Tu-160s launching from Ukrainka, while tactical aviation activity has increased on southern, northeastern, and southeastern fronts with KAB launches on Kharkivshchyna and Donetschynna. The loss of a Ukrainian F-16 on a combat interception mission on July 29, 2026 indicates active air-to-air engagements and potential vulnerabilities in Ukrainian air defense coordination. The combination of mass drone and missile threats with strategic bomber redeployments suggests Russia is attempting to overwhelm Ukrainian defenses through sheer volume and multi-domain pressure.
